rag-q61.testing: synthetic generation plus human curation, stratification, and a controlled experiment with statistics.
rag-q61.trap: a purely synthetic set, or judging a chunking change end-to-end only.
rag-q61.spoken:
"I'd build it in two passes: generate for volume, curate for trust.

Generation: sample chunks across the corpus, stratified by document type and section, and have an LLM write questions each chunk answers, with a reference answer. That automatically gives a relevance label: the source chunk. I ask for varied question types — factual lookups, multi-part, comparison, and unanswerable ones — because a set of easy lookups flatters every system. Multi-hop questions come from pairs of related chunks.

Curation: synthetic questions are too literal — they reuse the chunk's words — so domain experts review a sample: fix or drop bad questions, check reference answers, add questions in real users' language. As soon as there's any traffic or a pilot, real queries from logs are labelled and added, especially failures. I stratify: enough items per query type and document type to measure each slice, and I version the set.

Then the chunking change. I build a parallel index with the new chunker and keep everything else frozen — same embedding model, retriever settings, reranker, prompt and generator. Chunk-based labels break when chunks change, so I label relevance at the document-span level, or re-map source spans to new chunks. I read retrieval first: recall@k on both indexes, then end-to-end faithfulness and correctness, per slice. A paired test on the same questions tells me if the difference is real before I switch."

stages.name: Clarify
stages.html: • Decisions: chunking, embedding, reranker, prompt changes. Slices: query types, document types, languages, unanswerable.

stages.name: Generate for volume
stages.html:
Item type How
factual lookup question from one chunk
multi-hop question needing two linked chunks
comparison question across two documents
unanswerable plausible question the corpus doesn't answer
paraphrased rewrite to avoid chunk wording

stages.name: Curate for trust
stages.claim: experts and real queries make it trustworthy
stages.html: • Expert review of a sample (drop ambiguous/wrong items, fix references); add real queries and failures; record source spans, not only chunk IDs.

stages.name: Deep-dive
stages.html:
💻 Prove it — is a 6-point recall gain real? (McNemar on paired outcomes):

import math
base = [1]*140 + [0]*60          # recall@10 hits on 200 golden questions, old chunker
new  = base[:]                   # new chunker: fixes 18 misses, breaks 6 hits
for i in range(140, 158): new[i] = 1
for i in range(0, 6): new[i] = 0
b = sum(1 for x, y in zip(base, new) if x == 1 and y == 0); c = sum(1 for x, y in zip(base, new) if x == 0 and y == 1)
chi2 = (abs(b - c) - 1) ** 2 / (b + c)                       # McNemar with continuity correction
print(sum(base) / 200, sum(new) / 200, b, c, round(chi2, 2), "significant at 0.05" if chi2 > 3.84 else "not significant")
# → 0.7 0.76 6 18 5.04 significant at 0.05

Only the 24 questions that changed outcome matter; 18 fixed vs 6 broken is significant here. Still inspect the 6 regressions.

stages.name: Failure modes
stages.html: • Synthetic questions too literal (inflate dense recall); chunk-ID labels invalid after re-chunking; changing two things at once; no slice analysis; eval set leaking into prompts.

stages.name: Keep it alive
stages.html: • Monthly additions from production failures; retire stale items when documents change; version the set with the corpus snapshot it was built on.

followUps.question: 🧪 Your labels are chunk IDs. You re-chunk. What breaks and how do you fix it?
followUps.html: The IDs no longer exist, so recall can't be computed. Store source spans (document + character or section range) and count a new chunk as relevant if it overlaps the span.

followUps.question: "Synthetic questions are enough."
followUps.html: They're too literal and too easy, overstating dense retrieval. Human curation and real queries are what make the set trustworthy.

followUps.question: How many questions?
followUps.html: Enough per slice to detect the effect size that matters with a paired test — often a few hundred overall to start, growing toward thousands with production data.

followUps.question: Why freeze everything else?
followUps.html: So a difference is attributable to the chunker. Changing the embedder or prompt at the same time makes the result uninterpretable.

followUps.question: Retrieval improved but end-to-end didn't. Now what?
followUps.html: Look at context size and assembly: new chunks may be longer (more tokens, lost in the middle) or split tables differently. Check generation-side metrics and adjust generation k before deciding.

dontSay: A decision without a paired test.

rag-q62.testing: that code froze but data, queries, truth and dependencies kept moving — and signals per drift type.
rag-q62.trap: "nothing changed" because there were no deploys.
rag-q62.spoken:
"No deploys doesn't mean nothing changed. Four things keep moving.

The corpus: new documents arrived — sometimes in formats the parser handles badly — old versions weren't retired, so contradictions grew, and some sources stopped syncing. The queries: users now ask about new products, new features or seasonal topics that the corpus or the golden set doesn't cover. The truth: policies and prices changed, so answers that were right six months ago are wrong now even if retrieval works perfectly. And dependencies: a hosted model or embedding API may have been updated behind the same name, and the index may have degraded — soft deletes piling up, or index parameters no longer suited to its size.

To find which, I'd compare now against six months ago: the retrieval-score distribution for top results, abstention and empty-result rates, ingestion lag and parse error rates by source, query topic clusters versus the golden set, and a fresh run of the golden set. Then sample recent complaints and assign each to a pipeline stage.

The monitoring that would have caught it earlier: continuous reference-free scoring — groundedness and context relevance — on sampled traffic; retrieval-score distribution drift alerts; ingestion freshness and parse-failure alerts per source; topic clustering of new queries with coverage checks; scheduled golden-set runs; and a check that model versions are pinned."

stages.name: Name it
stages.claim: drift in data, queries, truth or dependencies
stages.html:
Drift Example
corpus new doc formats, stale versions, broken sync
query new products/topics not covered
truth policies changed; old answers now wrong
dependency provider model or embedding API updated; index degradation

stages.name: Rule out the fakes
stages.html:
• Expectations rose (users compare with newer tools) — check complaint specifics.
  • A few loud complaints vs a real metric shift — compare feedback rates.

stages.name: Confirm with evidence
stages.claim: compare then and now, per signal
stages.html:
💻 Prove it — the comparison table (cells to measure, now vs 6 months ago):

Signal Then Now Points to
golden-set recall@20 / groundedness measure measure retrieval / generation drift
top-1 retrieval score median measure measure embedding or corpus drift
abstention / empty-result rate measure measure coverage gaps, ingestion
ingestion lag, parse errors per source measure measure corpus drift
share of queries in uncovered topic clusters measure measure query drift
model version served measure measure dependency drift

stages.name: Fix
stages.html:
• Corpus: fix sync/parsing, supersede old versions, compact the index.
  • Queries: add content for new topics; extend the golden set.
  • Truth: re-index changed sources; add effective dates.
  • Dependencies: pin versions; re-run evals on any provider change.

stages.name: Monitoring that catches it earlier
stages.html: • Sampled reference-free scoring, score-distribution drift, freshness and parse alerts, topic coverage, scheduled golden-set runs, version pinning.

followUps.question: 🧪 Top-1 retrieval scores dropped by 0.1 on the same day for all queries, no deploy. Likely cause?
followUps.html: A dependency change: the embedding API or model behind a stable name was updated, so queries are embedded in a slightly different space from the stored vectors. Check provider changelogs; pin versions; re-embed if needed.

followUps.question: "No deploys, so it's user perception."
followUps.html: Data, queries, truth and dependencies change without deploys. Measure before dismissing.

followUps.question: What is reference-free scoring good for here?
followUps.html: It runs on live traffic without labels (groundedness, context relevance), so it tracks trends continuously; reference-based golden-set runs confirm on a fixed benchmark.

followUps.question: How do you detect query drift?
followUps.html: Cluster recent query embeddings and compare the cluster distribution with the golden set and past traffic; new clusters with high abstention are coverage gaps.

followUps.question: Who should get which alert?
followUps.html: Ingestion and parse alerts to the data/platform team; retrieval drift to the retrieval owners; coverage gaps to content owners; dependency changes to whoever owns model versions. Drift is cross-team, so ownership must be explicit.
